Title: Timing of Power of All vs Direct Intervention

Messages.Author: librarian
Messages.Body:
If someone plays a card, and one meth wants to play DI, and another
wants to play Power of All (both library card cancelers), whose card
play gets precedence?

Is it:

a) DI because it's a master card
b) Power of All because it's a minion card
c) clockwise around table from acting meth
d) resolve simultaneously
e) something I haven't listed here

In the case of a,b, and c, I assume that then the other player who's
card would play second, can't.

My guess is C. (or E)

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Almost.

If two or more players want to play a card or effect, the acting Methuselah
plays first. At every stage, the acting player always has the opportunity to
play the next card or effect. So after playing one effect, she may play another
and another. Once she is finished, the opportunity passes to the defending
Methuselah (in the cases of directed actions and combat), then to the rest of
the Methuselahs in clockwise order from the acting Methuselah. [1.6.1.5]

So if the card in play is played during a (D) action, then the target Methuselah
has first chance to play.

(The "combat" bit doesn't apply here, since Power of All isn't playable in
combat, but if it were a question of two DI's, then the combatant would get
first chance to cancel.)
